ownership.quote: GitHub, headquartered in San Francisco, is operated by Github, Inc., a subsidiary of Microsoft since 2018.

stage.quote: On June 4, 2018, Microsoft announced its intent to acquire GitHub for US$7.5 billion... The deal closed on October 26, 2018.
stage.note: GitHub Actions is a feature/product line of GitHub, Inc., which has been a wholly owned subsidiary of Microsoft (a public company) since October 2018. Before acquisition GitHub had raised a Series B round in 2015; that pre-acquisition history is no longer the relevant funding stage for this product.

total_funding_usd.basis: Sum of GitHub's disclosed pre-acquisition VC rounds: $100M (2012, a16z) + $250M Series B (2015, led by Sequoia Capital). GitHub was then acquired outright by Microsoft in 2018, ending independent fundraising.
total_funding_usd.quote: In July 2012... Andreessen Horowitz invested $100 million in venture capital with a $750 million valuation. In July 2015 GitHub raised another $250 million... in a series B round. The lead investor was Sequoia Capital...

last_round.quote: Microsoft announced its intent to acquire GitHub for US$7.5 billion (~$9.2 billion in 2024). The deal closed on October 26, 2018.

revenue.basis: Microsoft-disclosed figure for GitHub as a whole (not GitHub Actions specifically), reported by TechCrunch.
revenue.quote: Microsoft says GitHub now has a $1B ARR, 90M active users

note: GitHub Actions is a CI/CD feature of GitHub, which has been a wholly owned subsidiary of Microsoft since October 2018 ($7.5B acquisition). Not independently funded or reporting revenue; figures above are for GitHub as a whole, not GitHub Actions specifically. Revenue for parent Microsoft is reported in its 10-K but does not break out GitHub or GitHub Actions.
